articles.title: Netherlands Seizes 800 Servers, Arrests 2 for Aiding Cyberattacks
articles.summary: Meta's AI support bot got social engineered into handing over Obama's Instagram account to pro-Iranian trolls. When your chatbot has better access controls than your admins, maybe it's time to rethink the whole 'AI will solve security' narrative.

articles.title: Alleged Kimwolf Botmaster ‘Dort’ Arrested, Charged in U.S. and Canada
articles.summary: CISA contractor dumped AWS GovCloud keys on public GitHub because apparently the agency tasked with protecting America's infrastructure can't protect their own credentials. Congress is predictably outraged, but we're just impressed by the irony.

articles.title: We're Fighting Mass Surveillance Tech—and Winning
articles.summary: A CISA contractor left government cloud credentials exposed on GitHub for the world to see. The same agency telling everyone else about cybersecurity best practices just got schooled in 'don't commit your secrets, dipshit.'

articles.title: Attackers Use AI to Automate EDR Evasion Testing
articles.summary: License plate readers have evolved from catching speeders to full-spectrum surveillance creep—now tracking school residency and noise complaints. Because nothing says 'land of the free' like automated tracking of every car movement for trivial violations.

articles.title: Philly Cops Admit That They’re Tracking “First Amendment Activity” Critical of AI
articles.summary: Pentagon runs AI propaganda mill targeting Latin America while simultaneously crying about foreign disinformation campaigns. The cognitive dissonance is so thick you could cut it with a drone strike authorization.

articles.title: Commvault says it's time to rethink resiliency as AI crooks leave victims in a 'dark, dead' state
articles.summary: Philadelphia cops admit they're surveilling 'First Amendment activity' critical of AI data centers. Apparently exercising constitutional rights about corporate surveillance is now itself subject to surveillance.

articles.title: UK banks offered access to OpenAI’s GPT-5.5 amid exclusion from Anthropic’s Glasswing expansion
articles.summary: Security researchers are following Nightmare Eclipse's lead and instant-dropping Microsoft exploits instead of playing nice with Redmond's broken disclosure process. When the vendor won't listen, sometimes you have to get their attention with a digital brick through the window.

articles.title: Autonomous AI Tool Finds 2-Year-Old RCE Flaw in Redis (CVE-2026-23479)
articles.summary: Microsoft left debug flags enabled in production Office 365 Android apps, letting any app steal authentication tokens. It's like leaving your house keys under the doormat, except the doormat is labeled 'PRODUCTION BUILD.'

articles.title: In bed with Andrew Sa
articles.summary: Autonomous AI tool found a 2-year-old RCE flaw in Redis that humans missed entirely. The machines are officially better at finding bugs than we are—at least until they start hiding them for the robot uprising.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Oracle WebLogic flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: Oracle WebLogic CVE-2024-21182 added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after active exploitation in the wild. Another day, another enterprise Java framework getting owned by script kiddies.
